clean_source_blocks.text: A daredevil social media free-climber nicknamed the "Spider-Man of Yemen" has died after falling into a volcanic crater in the country's south-west. Al-Qaqa Ibn Antar had been attempting to climb its steep rock faces on Friday without safety equipment when he fell in, according to local authorities. The 30-year-old had a large following on social media and was well known for performing daring acrobatic stunts in online videos. The Hardah Dam volcanic crater is one of the country's most famous natural landmarks. Video footage appearing to show the moment of the fall has been widely circulating online. It shows Antar climbing the near-vertical wall of the crater before appearing to lose his grip and fall.

A popular Yemeni free climber celebrated as “Yemen’s Spider-Man” has died after plunging into a 120-metre (approximately 393-foot) volcanic crater during a daring ascent without any safety equipment. Al-Qa’qa’ bin Antar (also referred to as Qaqaa Antar al-Absi or similar spellings), known for his viral videos of equipment-free stunts, lost his footing while scaling the Haradhat Damt (or Hadrat Damt) volcanic crater in the Damt area of Yemen’s southern Al Dhale (Dhale) province.

original_article.research:
[Lähde: BBC World]
A daredevil social media free-climber nicknamed the "Spider-Man of Yemen" has died after falling into a volcanic crater in the country's south-west.

Al-Qaqa Ibn Antar had been attempting to climb its steep rock faces on Friday without safety equipment when he fell in, according to local authorities.

The 30-year-old had a large following on social media and was well known for performing daring acrobatic stunts in online videos.

The Hardah Dam volcanic crater is one of the country's most famous natural landmarks.

Video footage appearing to show the moment of the fall has been widely circulating online.

It shows Antar climbing the near-vertical wall of the crater before appearing to lose his grip and fall.

Yemen's Civil Defence Authority praised the "heroic efforts" of its water rescue team for successfully recovering Antar's body "from the bottom of the crater" in a statement issued on Sunday.

It described the operation over the weekend as "highly dangerous", and "one of the most difficult and complex field rescue missions".

It said the team had been promoted after demonstrating "exceptional field capabilities amid rugged terrain, harsh environmental conditions and high temperatures inside the volcanic crater".

It produced footage showing rescuers scaling down the side of the crater using climbing equipment, before winching a cage down to recover the climber's body.

His body was found by divers inside the 120m-wide crater at a depth of 30m (98ft) below the water surface, according to the Associated Press.

The Hardah Dam in Dhale province has become somewhat of a tourist attraction in recent years, with a hot sulfur lake sitting at its base.

---

Al-Qa’qa’ bin Antar (also referred to as Qaqaa Antar al-Absi or similar spellings), known for his viral videos of equipment-free stunts, lost his footing while scaling the Haradhat Damt (or Hadrat Damt) volcanic crater in the Damt area of Yemen’s southern Al Dhale (Dhale) province.

The incident occurred on or around June 12, 2026. Shocking footage captured the moment the climber lost his grip mid-ascent, sending him falling into the sulfur-filled crater as onlookers watched in horror. Local reports and civil defence updates confirm he attempted the climb without ropes, harnesses, or protective gear — a signature element of his high-risk style. He was often seen climbing barefoot and performing stunts inside the crater.

payload.title: Jemeniläinen vapaakiipeilijä kuoli pudottuaan tulivuorikraatteriin
payload.summary: Sosiaalisessa mediassa tunnettu jemeniläinen vapaakiipeilijä Al-Qaqa Ibn Antar kuoli pudottuaan Hardah Damin tulivuorikraatteriin Jemenin eteläosassa. Viranomaisten mukaan hän kiipesi ilman turvavarusteita.
payload.content:
Sosiaalisessa mediassa rohkeista tempuistaan tunnettu jemeniläinen vapaakiipeilijä Al-Qaqa Ibn Antar on kuollut pudottuaan tulivuorikraatteriin Jemenin eteläosassa. Paikallisten viranomaisten mukaan 30-vuotias Antar oli perjantaina kiipeämässä Hardah Damin kraatterin jyrkkiä kallioseinämiä ilman turvavarusteita, kun hän menetti otteensa ja putosi kraatteriin.

## Tunnettu vaarallisista kiipeilyvideoista

Antar tunnettiin verkossa lempinimellä Jemenin Spider-Man. Hänellä oli suuri seuraajajoukko sosiaalisessa mediassa, jossa hän julkaisi videoita akrobaattisista ja vaarallisista tempuistaan. Hänen julkinen maineensa perustui erityisesti nousuihin ja liikkeisiin, joita hän teki ilman tavanomaisia turvaköysiä tai muita varusteita.

Viranomaisten mukaan turmakohtana oli Hardah Damin tulivuorikraatteri, jota kuvataan yhdeksi Jemenin tunnetuimmista luonnonnähtävyyksistä. Kraatteri sijaitsee maan eteläisessä Dhaleen maakunnassa. Sen syvyydeksi on kerrottu noin 120 metriä eli noin 393 jalkaa.

## Putoamishetkestä levisi video

Tapausta koskevaa videomateriaalia on levinnyt laajasti verkossa. Kuvien kerrotaan näyttävän, kuinka Antar kiipeää lähes pystysuoraa kraatterin seinämää pitkin ennen kuin hän näyttää menettävän otteensa ja putoavan. Paikallinen pelastusviranomainen julkaisi lyhyen videon, jonka on kerrottu näyttävän putoamishetken.

Lähteissä Antarin nimen kirjoitusasu vaihtelee jonkin verran. Häneen viitataan myös muodoilla Al-Qa’qa’ bin Antar ja Qaqaa Antar al-Absi, mutta tiedot koskevat samaa jemeniläistä vapaakiipeilijää. Myös kraatterin nimestä esiintyy eri kirjoitusasuja, kuten Haradhat Damt ja Hadrat Damt.

## Viranomaiset kuvasivat tapahtuman kulun

Lähteissä toistuva kuvaus tapahtuneesta on sama: Antar kiipesi kraatterin jyrkkää seinämää ilman turvavarusteita, menetti otteensa ja putosi kraatteriin. Lähteissä ei kerrota muista osallisista. Tapaus nousi kansainvälisiin uutisiin erityisesti Antarin sosiaalisen median tunnettuuden ja putoamisesta levinneen videomateriaalin vuoksi.

Viranomaisten mukaan hän kiipesi ilman turvavarusteita.
